title: Using Toolbox Utilities

children:
The following is a comprehensive list of all the "Toolbox Utilities" 
 that are shipped with the application. In general, the purpose of these 
 utilities is to quickly perform a function in SCALE or a third-party application. 
 These are especially helpful if for some reason you need to add/manipulate 
 data outside of the application. You can access the Toolbox on the application server: Start 
 | All Programs | Manhattan Associates | ILS | Tools. You can also 
 access the toolbox by navigating to the following path on your application 
 server:          \\AppServer\ILS\, and 
 opening the file "ILSToolbox.exe"
**IMPORTANT** - Please run the SCALE Toolbox as an Administrative user.

WARNING! Do not use these utilities 
 unless you are a Manhattan representative, OR you are absolutely sure 
 of the consequences of executing a certain utility. Key application data 
 could be lost by the misuse of toolbox utilities.

NOTE: These "data loading" utilities are to be used for generating test data quickly. They are not meant to be used in a production environment for any purpose (with the exception of the Generic Config and Security utilities).
Run Web Stats For Multiple Days

You can use this utility to create shipping containers based 
 on the allocation requests that are already in the database. This can be helpful to create containers when a wave fails prior to work creation.
Creates a single container with multiple details, if the details have the same packing class.
Creates separate containers, if the details have different packing classes.
Puts the created container in an In Packing status.

The wave number you enter must 
 be a valid wave in the system. So, if you want to test only a few 
 allocation requests and put them on a test wave, be sure to create a new 
wave (with no shipments assigned) in the Wave Insight screen.
Enter an existing wave number into the field.
Press the Create Containers Button. The utility will create containers in the SCALE database based on the allocation requests that already exist for the associated wave.

You can use this utility to create a range of customers and/or 
 ship to's. Note that one record each for customer/company combination
Enter a range of customer numbers.
Enter a range of ship to numbers.
Select the company(s) that you want to associate with these new customers/ship to's.
- If you choose United States as a country, the appropriate postal codes will be derived from the state(s) you choose.
- If you choose a country that is not United States, you will need to enter in a postal code range.
Press the Create Button. The system will create the appropriate customer/ship to value(s) in the CUSTOMER database table.
Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
Address Line 1 is populated by the Customer ID followed by the text "customer creator";
City is populated by the text "City".

You can use this utility to create the SQL code required to create a new SCALE generic configuration 
 window.
Enter a Record Type and Description.
Define the "system value" fields that you want to appear on the System Defined Values tab of your generic configuration.
Define the "user value" fields that you want to appear on the User Defined Values of your generic configuration.

Press the Generate SQL Button to have the system create the SQL code required to create the new generic configuration. You will then need to execute this SQL in a query application in order to actually create the generic configuration record in the database.
Press the Clear SQL Button to delete any SQL code in the toolbox window.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
You can use this utility to adjust inventory into an existing, empty location or range of locations. Essentially, this utility performs the same function as the SCALE Inventory Adjustment screen.
- This utility does not allow you to create inventory for lot controlled items and items that are serial number tracked through inventory.
- This utility does not allow you to add inventory to license plate tracked locations.

- This utility will assign the item to a location in the order it cycles through them. For example, suppose you chose seven different items and seven different locations, and that the quantity range is set at a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100:
In the Location fields, provide location ID value or range of values.
In the Quantity Adjustment fields, enter the quantity range and unit of measure that you want to adjust.
In the Item/Company fields, select the item(s) that you want to adjust.
Press the Adjust Inventory Button to adjust the inventory quantity into the location(s). The data is placed into the LOCATION_INVENTORY database table.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
You can use this utility to create a new item record, and assign permanent locations and units of measure to this item. Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE
Enter the item or range of items that you want to create.
Use the tab fields to indicate the details of the item you are going to create.

- Note that on the Values tab, when you enter minimum/maximum values for cost/price fields, the system will as a result assign a random price value (chosen as a number between these two values) for these fields on the new Item record.
Enter values into the Item Location Assignment tab if you want to assign a permanent location to this item.
Enter values into the Item Unit of Measure tab if you want to create quantity unit of measures for this item.

Use the Quantity of Each Permutation to be Grouped Together Field to indicate that you want the system to create a number of different permutations of the same item (i.e. company, allocation rule, NMFC). Therefore, if there is a value in this field, the system will loop through that many times, and try to create that number of different permutations (with different company based on the company values that are selected in that check list box). Once the system reaches the number of permutations indicated, it will move onto the next item and repeat this process.

Press the Create Button to create the item records. The data will be placed into the ITEM, ITEM_LOCATION_ASSIGNMENT, and ITEM_UNIT_OF_MEASURE database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple item records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

You can use this utility to create receipts and/or receipt lines.  Note that this utility will allow you to create receipt lines that do not match the receipt's company designation. This can cause problems when processing receipts created with this utility.
Use the General Setup fields to enter the receipt information.
- The Receipt Prefix ID Field indicates the alphanumeric string you want to appear at the beginning of your receipt IDs.
Use the Receipts/Details fields to enter in how many receipts you want to create, and how many lines you want on each of these receipts.

- The Receipt ID Start Index Field indicates the number that will be added to the end of the IDs of your receipt(s). For example, if your receipt prefix ID was "TEST", and your start index was "2", if you created three receipts, they would be named "TEST-2", "TEST-3", and "TEST-4."
- Note that the system will randomly choose a number of lines that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.
Assign vendor/ship from/company value(s) for the receipt(s).
Select the item(s) you want to include on your receipt(s).

- Press the Non Item Master Item Button to add item(s) that are not defined in SCALE to your receipt(s). You will be able to enter the item ID, description, cost, list price, and net price for these items. After you provide this data, the non item master item will be displayed in the item list and available for selection.
- Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity value that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.

Press the Create Receipts Button to create the receipt(s). The data will be placed into the RECEIPT_HEADER and RECEIPT_DETAIL database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple receipt records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
You can use this utility to perform actions on security permissions records.  Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE
configuration. The data this utility affects is from the SECURITY database table.

Use the Copy Security function to copy the existing security permissions of one user to another existing user. The system will copy the permissions from the user selected in the drop-down field to the user(s) who are selected in the checkbox list.
Use the Grant Security function to allow a user access to the Security Permissions Window.
Use the Remove Security function to delete any security record(s) that exist for a user.
You can use this utility to create shipments and/or lines.  Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE

Screens. Note that this utility will allow you to create shipment lines that do not match the shipment's company designation. This can cause problems when processing shipments created with this utility.
Use the General Setup fields to enter the shipment information.
- The Shipment Prefix ID Field indicates the alphanumeric string you want to appear at the beginning of your shipment IDs.

Use the Shipments/Details fields to enter in how many shipments you want to create, and how many details you want on each of these shipments. Note that the system will randomly choose a number of details that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.

- The Shipment ID Start Index Field indicates the number that will be added to the end of the IDs of your shipment(s). For example, if your shipment prefix ID was "TEST", and your start index was "2", if you created three shipments, they would be named "TEST-2", "TEST-3", and "TEST-4."
Assign a customer/ship to/company value(s) for the shipment(s).
Select the carrier /carrier service you want associated with the shipment(s).
Select the item(s) you want to include on your shipment(s).

- Press the Non Item Master Item Button to add item(s) that are not defined in SCALE to your shipment(s). You will be able to enter the item ID, description, cost, list price, and net price for these items. After you provide this data, the non item master item will be displayed in the item list and available for selection.
- Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity value that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.
Choose if you want to create shipments, orders, or both.

Press the Create Shipments Button to create the shipment(s). The data will be placed into the SHIPMENT_HEADER/SHIPMENT_DETAIL and/or the ORDER_HEADER/ORDER_DETAIL database tables (depending on what you selected in step 6). Note that when the tool creates multiple shipment records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.
Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

You can use this utility to create work based on an existing 
 wave. Note that the system will automatically detect what type of work it should be generating. This is based on the wave flow associated with the "launch number" (wave number) which you key-in to generate the work. This utility is helpful if you need to create work for a wave that has failed prior to the work creation wave step.

You can use this utility to upgrade both the SCALE application 
 and system databases. The 
 upgrade can be from a base release to service pack, a service pack to 
 a base release, and a base release to the next base release. You can compare the environments in the list to the version listed in the header portion of the window to see if the environment(s) needs updating.
Version: This field Indicates the release version of SCALE.
Service Pack: This field is not currently supported.
Build:  This field indicates the build number installed.
Environment: This field indicates the environment database(s) configured in SCALE.
Database: This field is not currently supported.
Version: This field indicates the release version of SCALE that the environment database is on.
Build: This indicates the build number the environment's database is on.
Type: This field indicates the type of database (it will always be "SQL Server").
Unicode: This field indicates that the database supports Unicode (the value will always be "Yes" now).
Start Services: This action starts the ILS Services and IIS.
Stop Services: This action stops the ILS Services and IIS.
Reset Services: This action stops and starts the ILS Services and IIS.
Refresh Grid Data: This action reloads the grid’s list of databases.
Upgrade Button: Select an environment from the record list that you want to upgrade, and press the Upgrade Button.

You can use this utility to view the following license 
 key values: BIOS serial number, machine name, and MAC addresses. This utility performs the same functionality as the System Information Tab of the SCALE
Press the Go Button to display the license key values.

You can use this utility to change the default database that the application points 
 to (the system will change the setting in the wmfw.config 
 file). Note that other databases (if they exist) are still managed through the Environment configuration in SCALE. Also note that the Oracle option is no longer supported.
Data Source: This field indicates the machine name where the SQL Server database resides.
Catalog: This field indicates the database name.
User / Password: These fields indicate the logon information for the data source.
Multi Byte Checkbox: This setting indicates Unicode support (you should always select this checkbox).
You can use this utility to perform several functions that deal with the resource files:
Select XML as the Export Type.
Select the Table (RESOURCE_FILE_BASE or RESOURCE_FILE_CUSTOM) from which to export.
Select the Culture Name to export.
Enter a new file name or use the default file name.
Name the spreadsheet based on the release, language and region/country (e.g.,
Select Data | From Other Sources | From XML Data Import.
Browse to location and select the XML file saved during the Export to XML steps.
Excel will display the warning, “The specified XML source does not refer to a schema.  Excel will create a schema based on the XML source data.”
Excel will prompt to Import Data.
Select the XML table in existing worksheet option.  The value $A$1 should be defaulted in the text box.
Convert the spreadsheet to a ‘trp’ file using the following steps.
a. Delete all columns except for the Resource Key, Resource Group and Text columns.
b. Delete the blank rows between the column header names and the first resource key.
c. Arrange the columns in Resource Key, Resource Group and Text order.

f. Insert a new column between the Group and Translation Text columns.
g. Name the new column English Text.
Rename the file extension from ‘xlsx’ to ‘trp’.
Import the ‘trp’ file into SCALE using the Translation Wizard and the “Import Manhattan Associates base translated screen values” option.
The output of this export is saved in a proprietary format that can only be run by the application installer. Note that this option typically will not be used in a live client environment.

Select the Table (RESOURCE_FILE_BASE or RESOURCE_FILE_CUSTOM) from which to export.
Select the Culture Name to export.

This is only used for creating database scripts to be included and run by the application installer during an upgrade or product update.  The WMW Script file size is typically 10+ MB, which is too large to execute without timing out.  It is recommended this script be partitioned into 10 or more scripts that are less than 1 MB in size. Note that this option typically will not be used in a live client environment.

You can use this utility to change the version, service pack, and build level values that are stored in the VERSION database table. You can change these values both in the application and system databases.   The installer sets these values during the installation process. Typically, you would not need to manually update these values; however, this tool is helpful in the rare case where the installer does not update them, or if you want to re-run a set of scripts against the database (and then you want to set these values to an earlier build).

Database: This field indicates the database you want to view build information from (the application database or the system database). Note that the system database has information that is shared across environments.

You can use this utility to update the CARRIER_COMMITMENTS database table, with the system pulling data from a text file provided by the carrier. For example, suppose you need the delivery days for all zip codes from your origin (warehouse). Carrier(s) would then supply you a file with these days to deliver, and you would in turn need to update the CARRIER_COMMITMENTS table to reflect this. Note that you might need to change the format of the files you are supplied by the carrier, since this tool can only process delimited text files. In the delimited text file, you will need to specify the delimiter used in the file, and then just indicate which delimited field positions represent the Days to Deliver and Zip Code fields (these are the required fields, all other field positions will be ignored). This tool simply reads all of the records from the text file and then inserts them into the CARRIER_COMMITMENTS table.
Select a carrier and carrier service.
Select the carrier commitment file to upload.
Enter a path and file name for the output file that the system creates as part of this process. This file includes all the carrier commitment records in a comma delimited format.
Provide your warehouse's zip code in the Origin Zip Code field.

Select the Delete Only checkbox if you want to simply delete all the records in the CARRIER_COMMITMENTS table for this carrier/service and origin, and not perform any updates. In this case, you will only need to select this checkbox, a carrier, a carrier service, and press the GO Button. If you want the system to delete and then add records, you would not select this checkbox.
Use the Source File Options fields to indicate the delimiter that the carrier commitments file uses, and the positions of the Days to Deliver and Zip Code values in the records.
Note that this utility was created with the following values in mind:
The origin country is hard-coded as "US"
The destination country is hard-coded as "US"
The effective from date is hard-coded as 1/1/2001
The effective to date is hard-coded as 12/31/2999

children: You can use this utility to display and manipulate logical locks placed on database tables during such operations as locating or picking. This utility allows you to view and selectively release these record locks.
- Locating Note: Locations are locked from the locating process if the record in the LOCATION database table has a "Y" value for the LOCKED_FOR_LOCATE field.
- Work Instructions Note: Work instructions are locked from the picking process if the record in the WORK_INSTRUCTION database table has a "Y" value for the LOCKED field.

You can use this utility to advance the date values on application 
 database records to a future date. Note that this includes all dates in the database tables, including the DATE_TIME_STAMP field.
Enter the number of months that you want to advance database record dates by. For example, if you want the date to advance one year into the future, then you would enter 12 into this field.

You can use this utility to deactivate 
 inactive work instructions. Inactive 
 work is defined as work belonging to an entirely closed work unit (except 
 shipping work, which becomes inactive once the work unit's associated 
 shipment line(s) have all been load confirmed). When run, the system will move all closed 
 work to an inactive work database table (IA_WORK_INSTRUCTION).

You can use this utility to change the Form ID of a SCALE window in 
 the FORM database table. A Form ID is an internal numeric identifier of a screen used by the system to track its associated security. You could use this tool when you are creating a custom screen and then changing its Form ID to give it a value that is outside of the range of anything the base SCALE product would ever use (i.e., an arbitrarily high value). Note that when using this utility, the system will also make the appropriate changes in the SECURITY and SECURITY_CHECKPOINT database tables.

You can use this utility to adjust a range 
 of items into a range of warehouse locations. Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE Inventory Adjustment screen.
Use the Item tab to indicate what item/item range you would like to adjust. You can also indicate that you want item cross reference records for these items as well.
Use the Location tab to indicate either a number of general locations or a range of specific location IDs that you want to adjust the item(s) into.

Use the Adjustment Type/Quantity tab to indicate if you want to perform a positive/negative adjustment, and the quantity you want to adjust into these locations. Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.

Press OK to perform the adjustment. The system will make the appropriate changes to the LOCATION_INVENTORY table (and the ITEM _CROSS_REFERENCE table, if you chose to create cross references as well).

You can use this utility to view and delete cache records (which includes both data records and data locks). You can view the cache summary records on the grid. You can use this utility to troubleshoot data discrepancies between SCALE and the data actually contained in the database. This tool allows you to delete specific cache records, and therefore cause the data to be retrieved from the database again to resolve data issues, instead of running an ILSReset (which can be an invasive process).
If you select a cache record from the grid, then the system will display more details (if they exist) below the grid.
You can delete a cache record by right-clicking the grid. Note that you can only delete one record at a time. Also, you must have administrative rights to delete these records.
It is not recommended that you delete lock entries from the cache; however, the tool does not prevent this action.

You can use this utility to easily capture and export SCALE configuration data from one SCALE environment to another. Also, this utility has the ability to record changes  to SCALE configurations in the form of an installable package. These installable packages are an easy way to promote configuration data from a test environment to a production environment; or, to apply changes to multiple environments.
IMPORTANT NOTE: This utility uses the “SQL Server Change Data Capture (CDC)” functionality, which is not available in Azure SQL database. See your Manhattan representative for more details.

The Configuration Coordinator allows you to select a set of SCALE configuration records for a particular environment, and save it with a given name (called a “project”). There is no restriction on the number projects per SCALE environment.
Select an Existing Configuration Setup Field:
Press the New Button. The utility will open the Configuration Setup Window.
Provide a unique Project Name value, which identifies the project.
Provide a Description for the project.
Determine what data you want the utility to gather:
- Basic:The utility will gather data from *all* configurations.
- Advanced: You can select the configuration(s) that you want the utility to gather data from.
Press the Save Button. The utility will create the project.

NOTE: The utility also supports an extensible mechanism to ignore a specific change to a configuration record. These exclusions need to be defined manually in the CONFIG_DIR_TABLE_EXCLUSIONS database table.
All changes to the Shipment's "User Defined Field 1" and "User Defined Field 2" will be ignored by this utility.
The system is shipped with the following pre-defined exclusions:
Starting a project initiates the configuration change capture process, and records all of the changes made to SCALE configurations that are associated with the project.
Select an existing configuration project from the list.

Press the Start button. Note that the utility allows only one active project per environment. If the project does not have any historical data associated with it (i.e., it has not been run before), then the utility will start gathering data. If there is existing historical data, then proceed to step 3.
If you are attempting to start a project which has historical data associated with it, the utility will display a dialog where you can choose from a set of predefined actions:
- Append: The utility will append all new changes to any pre-existing data.
- Archive: The utility will move all pre-existing data to an archive table and continue to capture fresh changes.
- Delete: The utility will purge all pre-existing data and new changes will be captured.
- Cancel: No action will be taken.
You would stop a project after completing configuration changes.
Select a currently-running configuration project from the list.

Press  the Stop button. The utility will stop the data gathering process, and all configuration change information that has been recorded by the utility in SQL Server CDC tables will be moved to the CONFIG_DIR_COLLECTED_DATA database table.
The system writes process history for 3 different types of operations done to configurations:
Exporting a project allows you the ability to export the configuration data to a user-defined location. Run the SQL scripts directly using the SQL server management studio to export the data.
Provide a valid directory in the Export To Field.
Press the Export button. The utility will create the installer package with the configuration data.
Importing a project is the process of applying the configuration changes to a destination environment (single or multiple).
You can use this utility to configure several values related to configuring high availability. This utility supports multiple environments. You can configure the following settings:
“URL Load Balancer” defines the server name where the load balancer is located. Changing this value on the utility will update the technical value "URL Load Balancer Server Name".
“MSMQ Cluster” defines the MSMQ role’s ClientAccessPoint:
. Changing this value on the utility will update the technical value "MSMQ cluster". For more details, see the Message Queuing Guide.

“External Storage Path” indicates the path that is to be used as the defined storage location for several functional areas. Changing this value on the utility will update the corresponding configuration/database values that point the system to the file storage location, such as the server path values from the Technical Values or Web System Values configuration windows.

When SCALE is installed within an Azure IaaS Virtual Machine, Azure File Storage can be used to automatically provide high availability for files that are heavily used by the application (such as interface files, wave labels, and so on). "Azure storage connection string" stores the connection string for storing this information in Azure.

Note that when the external storage path is used as an Azure file storage path (for example, https://sgfsnode.file.core.windows.net/ils), the word ‘ils’ in this path should always be mentioned in small letters.

You can use this utility to search though all 
 documents in a specified directory, and find/replace a text string. This utility supports any document that can be successfully opened into Windows Notepad.
Provide the Old and New text values.
Provide the directory where the file(s) reside.
Select the Recursive checkbox if you want this utility to search in documents that reside in subdirectories.
Press the Replace Button. The system will replace the "old" text value with the "new" text value.

You can use this utility to gather detailed system related data for every server in your SCALE environment (application and database). The resulting data can then be sent to Manhattan for further analysis. This utility collects several trace files that can be helpful in monitoring the SCALE application. The tool places the trace file output in the following directory:
. In this directory will be a folder for each trace run, suffixed with the date/time of the run (e.g., Trace_20120808143215).
The following trace related data is captured by this tool:
Windows Performance Monitor traces for each active server defined in the grid on the screen, based on the Performance Monitor template specified. Two standard server templates (
) are provided to gather the Windows Performance Monitor data. These templates are stored on your application server in the following location:
. The resulting trace file output will be stored within a folder for each server name (e.g., <Server1> through <ServerN>), underneath the trace output folder structure mentioned above.

SQL Profiler traces for long running queries, blocked processes, and deadlocks. The resulting trace file output will be stored within the Database Information folder underneath the trace output folder structure mentioned above.

SQL Server output for various recommended configuration settings, index fragmentation and usage, and table sizes. The resulting trace file output will be stored within the Database Information folder underneath the trace output folder structure mentioned above.

SCALE activity output for different points in time during the trace run. The resulting trace file output will be stored within the Database Information folder underneath the trace output folder structure mentioned above.
Create entries in the grid for each SCALE-related server you want the Windows Performance Monitor traces to be captured. The tool will remember the grid settings.
Activate each server you want to be included in the trace.
Press the Start button to start the trace.
The trace must be manually stopped. Press the Stop button to stop the trace.

Caution should be used when using this utility in a production environment. Only experienced IT staff or Manhattan Representatives should be allowed to run this tool. Use toolbox security and the Windows administrative rights mentioned below to control who can run the tool.

You can use this utility to generate SQL script files in order create custom metadata screens, and activate/deactivate/delete these screens. This is helpful, if, for example, you want to create a specialized version of an Insight screen.

This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a base (shipped) metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to create a specialized version of a base metadata screen. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).
Select the Base button (note that you cannot export custom screens).
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
Select the Metadata Screen you want to customize.

Press the Customize button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>.
- As part of the Customize action, the system also will execute the SQL script that was generated. This will create all the records in the appropriate metadata configuration tables in the database.

This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a customized metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to save a backup of a custom screen’s current state. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).
Select the Custom button (note that you cannot export base screens).
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
Select the Metadata Screen you want to export.

Press the Export button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>.
- This directory is created upon the first export action, not by the application installer.

- The system will append a suffix of “V1” to the file name, which indicates this is the first version of the script file for this metadata screen. When you perform an Export action again for this screen, the system will create another “version” of the SQL script file (V2, for example).
- The file name starts with the Form ID of the metadata screen that you exported.
- The system will always create a new version of a file when exporting, whether or not there have been changes made to the configurations since the last export of this screen.
This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen available for use on your production environment.
Select the Custom button (you cannot activate base screens).
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to activate.
Press the Activate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "Yes", and display a success message.

- Keep in mind that when you activate a custom screen, then the system will also deactivate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you activate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will deactivate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.
This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen not available for use on your production environment.
Select the Custom button (you cannot deactivate base screens).
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to deactivate.
Press the Deactivate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "No", and display a success message.

- Keep in mind that when you deactivate a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you deactivate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.
This action allows you to remove a customized metadata screen’s configuration records from the database.
Select the Custom button (you cannot delete base screens).
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to delete.

Press the Delete button.  The system will display a confirmation message, asking if you are sure you want to delete the screen. Once you confirm, the system will remove this screen’s configuration records from all of the appropriate database tables, and display a success message.

- Keep in mind that when you delete a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you delete a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.
- Also as part of this action, the system will generate a SQL Script file representing the deleted screen, so that you have a backup in case you want to restore it at a later time.
- The system does not delete any of the SQL script files that you have previously generated for a screen.

You can use this utility to launch the SQL Processor mini-application. The SQL Processor is used 
 to store SQL statements, run them, and save the results.

To create a 
 statement to be saved, select "--NEW--" from the Name 
 drop down box.  Fill 
 in the name, active flag, and SQL in the boxes.  Then 
 select the Add button.

To update a 
 statement, select the statement to be modified from the Name drop 
 down box.  The 
 SQL and active flag can be modified.  When 
 you are done with the modifications, select the Update button.

To delete a 
 statement, select the statement from the Name drop down box.  Select 
 the Delete Button.

To run a statement, 
 select the statement from the Name drop down box.  A 
 statement can also be typed into the SQL box without creating a statement. 
  Select 
 the Run button to execute the statement.

To save the 
 results of an executed statement, go to 'File->Save Results'. 
  A window 
 will open to let you choose the file path and name.

To save a group 
 of SQL statements to be loaded or run at a later date, select 'File->Save 
 SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name.

To load a set 
 of SQL statements, select 'File->Load SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name.

When running this application from the command line there are three 
 command options:

This option will open the application with the specified filename as 
 the .ini file.  If 
 this option is not used, the default of SQLProcessor.ini will be used.

This will open the application will the SQL statements in the specified 
 file preloaded.  If 
 no .sql file is specified, the application will be run with no preloaded 
 statements.

This will run the application in non-interactive mode.  When 
 in non-interactive mode, the application will run the loaded SQL statements. 
  The results 
 will be save according to the configurations set in the .ini file that 
 was specified.  If 
 there is no .sql file specified, no commands will be run.  The 
 results will be saved with the name of the command, the date, and the 
 time concatenated.  If 
 there is an error running the SQL statement, the error will be reported 
 in the file.  If 
 there was an error saving the file, it will be reported in "Error.txt" 
 in the same folder as the application. An example of invoking this is the following:  ilstoolbox 
 "SQL Processor" /sql  <filename> 
 /n NOTE: If you would like to store your SQL files in a location other 
 than where the ILSToolbox.exe is located you will need to indicate the 
 file path along with the file name when running the utility via the command 
 line.
Steps to Schedule queries on SQL processor

Create the SQL file through SQL processor which has to be scheduled.

Select New from the Name drop down and write the SQL query to be run in the text box. Give a name for the query in the text box under the ‘Name’ text box and Click Add.

If you have multiple queries, keep adding by clicking New and following the similar steps.
Once all the queries are added, click File | Save SQL and save the file.

For example, if there were 2 queries, the contents of the SQL file would look like this:
USERPROFILE SELECT * FROM USER_PROFILE (NOLOCK) Y ¬
Settings on SQL processor. Click the Settings tab, the SQL Processor Config UI comes up; Check the output type as CSV and click Save and Exit.

Copy the SQLProcessor.Default.ini file to folder where the SQL file was saved earlier. 
(Note that the default ini location is in isolated storage, where the path is like: C:\Documents and Settings\<username>\Local Settings\Application Data\IsolatedStorage\<gibberish>\<more gibberish>\StrongName.<yet even more gibberish>\AssemFiles\SQLProcessorFile.Default.ini. Or it could be found in user’s Document’s folder)

The Contents of the ini file would look like – 
 CSV,  which means the output file will be saved in csv format.

Create a batch file to run the SQL query using SQL processor. In the command, put the location of the ToolBox, then the location of the sql file which was created in Step 1. Specify the location of the ini file. The SQL processor will creates the output according to the ini file settings.

The command would be like this:

"C:\Program Files\Manhattan Associates\WarehouseMgt\wmtoolbox" "SQL Processor"

Create a scheduled task to run the batch file. Go to Control Panel->Scheduled Tasks-> Add new Scheduled Task.
The Scheduled Task Wizard comes up
.
Click Next. On the next window Click Browse and select the batch file you have created, Select the frequency at which this job has to be done and Click Next.
In the Next screen give the date and time at which it is required to run and Click Next.
On the next screen give the user name/ password information for which the task has to be run.
Click the Finish button in the next screen.
The queries will be run at the scheduled time and resulting CSV files will be saved in the same folder where the batch file is present with timestamp.

Using Toolbox Utilities
        The following is a comprehensive list of all the "Toolbox Utilities" 
 that are shipped with the application. In general, the purpose of these 
 utilities is to quickly perform a function in SCALE or a third-party application. 
 These are especially helpful if for some reason you need to add/manipulate 
 data outside of the application. You can access the Toolbox on the application server: Start 
 | All Programs | Manhattan Associates | ILS | Tools. You can also 
 access the toolbox by navigating to the following path on your application 
 server:          \\AppServer\ILS\, and 
 opening the file "ILSToolbox.exe"
         
        **IMPORTANT** - Please run the SCALE Toolbox as an Administrative user.
         
        WARNING! Do not use these utilities 
 unless you are a Manhattan representative, OR you are absolutely sure 
 of the consequences of executing a certain utility. Key application data 
 could be lost by the misuse of toolbox utilities.
         
         
        Utility Descriptions...
         
        Data Loading Utilities
            
                 
                NOTE: These "data loading" utilities are to be used for generating test data quickly. They are not meant to be used in a production environment for any purpose (with the exception of the Generic Config and Security utilities).
                 
                Containers
                
                Customers
                
                Generic Config
                
                Inventory
                
                Items
                
                Receipts
                
                Security
                
                Shipments
                
                Work
                
                 
            
        
         
         
        Data Manipulation Utilities
            
                 
                Carrier Commitment Updater
                
                Change System Value
                
                Clear Data
                
                Complete Wave
                
                Database Lock Manager
                
                Date Advancer
                
                Deactivate Inactive Work
                
                Form ID Adjuster
                
                Mass Inventory Adjuster
                
                 
            
        
         
        System Tools
            
                 
                Cache Manager
                
                Configuration Coordinator
                
                High Availability
                
                Replace Text Utility
                
                SCALE Performance Monitor
                
                 
            
        
         
        Testing
            
                 
                Interface Web Service Request Creator
                
                Integration Services Simulator
                
                Manifest Shipment Test
                
                Pack Container
                
                Receiving Verifier
                
                Run Web Stats For Multiple Days
                
                Shipping Load Confirm Test
                
                Simulate Inline Scanner
                
                 
            
        
         
        Development
            
                 
                Audit Log Viewer
                
                Constant List
                
                DBC Script Generator
                
                Debug Filter
                
                EPC Decoder
                
                Get Resource Text
                
                Metadata Screen Utility
                
                SQL Formatter
                
                SQL Processor
                
                SQL Worksheet
                
                System Config SQL Generator
                
                 
            
        
         
         
         Data Loading Utilities...
        Containers
         
        You can use this utility to create shipping containers based 
 on the allocation requests that are already in the database. This can be helpful to create containers when a wave fails prior to work creation.
         
        This Utility...
        
            Creates a single container with multiple details, if the details have the same packing class. 
            Creates separate containers, if the details have different packing classes.
            Puts the created container in an In Packing status.
            The wave number you enter must 
 be a valid wave in the system. So, if you want to test only a few 
 allocation requests and put them on a test wave, be sure to create a new 
wave (with no shipments assigned) in the Wave Insight screen.
        
        Procedures
        
            Enter an existing wave number into the field.
            Press the Create Containers Button. The utility will create containers in the SCALE database based on the allocation requests that already exist for the associated wave.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Customers
        You can use this utility to create a range of customers and/or 
 ship to's. Note that one record each for customer/company combination
        
            Enter a range of customer numbers.
            Enter a range of ship to numbers.
            Select the company(s) that you want to associate with these new customers/ship to's.
            Select the country:- If you choose United States as a country, the appropriate postal codes will be derived from the state(s) you choose.- If you choose a country that is not United States, you will need to enter in a postal code range.
            Press the Create Button. The system will create the appropriate customer/ship to value(s) in the CUSTOMER database table.Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
        
        Address Value Notes
        
            Address Line 1 is populated by the Customer ID followed by the text "customer creator"; Address Lines 2 & 3 are populated with NULL values.
            City is populated by the text "City".
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Generic Config
        You can use this utility to create the SQL code required to create a new SCALE generic configuration 
 window.
        
            Enter a Record Type and Description.
            Define the "system value" fields that you want to appear on the System Defined Values tab of your generic configuration. 
            Define the "user value" fields that you want to appear on the User Defined Values of your generic configuration.
            Press the Generate SQL Button to have the system create the SQL code required to create the new generic configuration. You will then need to execute this SQL in a query application in order to actually create the generic configuration record in the database.Press the Clear SQL Button to delete any SQL code in the toolbox window.Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Inventory
        You can use this utility to adjust inventory into an existing, empty location or range of locations. Essentially, this utility performs the same function as the SCALE Inventory Adjustment screen.
         
        Keep In Mind 
        - This utility does not allow you to create inventory for lot controlled items and items that are serial number tracked through inventory.

         
        - This utility does not allow you to add inventory to license plate tracked locations.
         
        - Remember that this utility will only adjust inventory into existing empty locations.
         
        - This utility will assign the item to a location in the order it cycles through them. For example, suppose you chose seven different items and seven different locations, and that the quantity range is set at a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100:
         
        
            
            
            
            
                
                    
                        Items

            In the Location fields, provide location ID value or range of values.
            In the Quantity Adjustment fields, enter the quantity range and unit of measure that you want to adjust.
            In the Item/Company fields, select the item(s) that you want to adjust.
            Press the Adjust Inventory Button to adjust the inventory quantity into the location(s). The data is placed into the LOCATION_INVENTORY database table.Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Items
        You can use this utility to create a new item record, and assign permanent locations and units of measure to this item. Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE Item, Item Unit of Measure, and Item Location Assignment configurations.
        
            Enter the item or range of items that you want to create.
            Use the tab fields to indicate the details of the item you are going to create. - Note that on the Values tab, when you enter minimum/maximum values for cost/price fields, the system will as a result assign a random price value (chosen as a number between these two values) for these fields on the new Item record.
            Enter values into the Item Location Assignment tab if you want to assign a permanent location to this item.
            Enter values into the Item Unit of Measure tab if you want to create quantity unit of measures for this item.
            Use the Quantity of Each Permutation to be Grouped Together Field to indicate that you want the system to create a number of different permutations of the same item (i.e. company, allocation rule, NMFC). Therefore, if there is a value in this field, the system will loop through that many times, and try to create that number of different permutations (with different company based on the company values that are selected in that check list box). Once the system reaches the number of permutations indicated, it will move onto the next item and repeat this process.
            Press the Create Button to create the item records. The data will be placed into the ITEM, ITEM_LOCATION_ASSIGNMENT, and ITEM_UNIT_OF_MEASURE database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple item records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen. Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Receipts
        You can use this utility to create receipts and/or receipt lines.  Note that this utility will allow you to create receipt lines that do not match the receipt's company designation. This can cause problems when processing receipts created with this utility.
        
            Use the General Setup fields to enter the receipt information.- The Receipt Prefix ID Field indicates the alphanumeric string you want to appear at the beginning of your receipt IDs.
            Use the Receipts/Details fields to enter in how many receipts you want to create, and how many lines you want on each of these receipts. - The Receipt ID Start Index Field indicates the number that will be added to the end of the IDs of your receipt(s). For example, if your receipt prefix ID was "TEST", and your start index was "2", if you created three receipts, they would be named "TEST-2", "TEST-3", and "TEST-4."- Note that the system will randomly choose a number of lines that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.
            Assign vendor/ship from/company value(s) for the receipt(s). 
            Select the item(s) you want to include on your receipt(s). - Press the Non Item Master Item Button to add item(s) that are not defined in SCALE to your receipt(s). You will be able to enter the item ID, description, cost, list price, and net price for these items. After you provide this data, the non item master item will be displayed in the item list and available for selection.- Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity value that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.
            Press the Create Receipts Button to create the receipt(s). The data will be placed into the RECEIPT_HEADER and RECEIPT_DETAIL database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple receipt records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

            Press the Confirm Button to have the system confirm the load(s).Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Simulate Inline Scanner
        This utility is built to simulate a scan and weigh system that posts close/manifest container requests at a timed interval. The system will first process all records found by the SQL statement and create scan and weigh request insert statements. Once the statements are written to the file, they will be read from the file again and posted to the database on a regular interval. You may reuse the same SQL statement file by leaving the SQL statement field blank and specifying an existing file. You must enter a SQL statement that returns SHIPMENT_ID and/or CONTAINER_ID and WEIGHT (as selected in the drop down list) in the respective order.
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        Development Utilities... 
         
        Audit Log Viewer
        You can use this utility to view the details 
 of a specific audit, and save it as a file. This utility performs a similar function to that of the SCALE Audit Log Insight Screen.
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        Constant List
        You can use this utility to view a list of all the constants from the source code.
         
        back to top
        
         
          
        DBC Script Generator
        You can use this utility to generate DBC_ stored procedures. These are then used to insert records that are shipped into the database.
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        Debug Filter
        You can use this utility to filter the results of a debug file.
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        EPC Decoder
        You can use this utility to display detailed information of an EPC code. See the topic How an EPC is Generated for more information about EPC codes.
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        Get Resource Text
        You can use this utility to retrieve the text of system "message strings" or "text strings" from the resource file. This utility performs some of the same functions as the SCALE System Text Editor.
        
            Enter a valid SCALE message code, such as MSG_WORK01.
            Indicate whether this code represents a message string (used for error/history messages) or a text string (used for field/button label text).
            Press the >> Button. The corresponding text will be displayed for the code you entered.
        
        back to top
        
         
         
        Metadata Screen Utility
        You can use this utility to generate SQL script files in order create custom metadata screens, and activate/deactivate/delete these screens. This is helpful, if, for example, you want to create a specialized version of an Insight screen. 
         
        Customizing a Base Metadata Screen
        This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a base (shipped) metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to create a specialized version of a base metadata screen. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).
        
            Select the Base button (note that you cannot export custom screens).
            Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
            Select the Metadata Screen you want to customize.
            Press the Customize button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>.Notes:- As part of the Customize action, the system also will execute the SQL script that was generated. This will create all the records in the appropriate metadata configuration tables in the database.
        
        Exporting a Custom Metadata Screen
        This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a customized metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to save a backup of a custom screen’s current state. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).
        
            Select the Custom button (note that you cannot export base screens).
            Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
            Select the Metadata Screen you want to export. 
            Press the Export button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>. Notes:- This directory is created upon the first export action, not by the application installer. - The system will append a suffix of “V1” to the file name, which indicates this is the first version of the script file for this metadata screen. When you perform an Export action again for this screen, the system will create another “version” of the SQL script file (V2, for example). - The file name starts with the Form ID of the metadata screen that you exported. - The system will always create a new version of a file when exporting, whether or not there have been changes made to the configurations since the last export of this screen.
        
        Activating a Customized Metadata Screen
        This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen available for use on your production environment.
        
             Select the Custom button (you cannot activate base screens).
            Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
            Select the Metadata Screen that you want to activate.
            Press the Activate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "Yes", and display a success message.Notes:- Keep in mind that when you activate a custom screen, then the system will also deactivate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you activate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will deactivate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.
        
        Deactivating a Customized Metadata Screen
        This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen not available for use on your production environment.
        
             Select the Custom button (you cannot deactivate base screens).
            Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
            Select the Metadata Screen that you want to deactivate.
            Press the Deactivate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "No", and display a success message.Notes:- Keep in mind that when you deactivate a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you deactivate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.
        
        Deleting a Customized Metadata Screen
        This action allows you to remove a customized metadata screen’s configuration records from the database.
        
            Select the Custom button (you cannot delete base screens).
            Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.
            Select the Metadata Screen that you want to delete.
            Press the Delete button.  The system will display a confirmation message, asking if you are sure you want to delete the screen. Once you confirm, the system will remove this screen’s configuration records from all of the appropriate database tables, and display a success message.Notes:- Keep in mind that when you delete a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you delete a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.- Also as part of this action, the system will generate a SQL Script file representing the deleted screen, so that you have a backup in case you want to restore it at a later time.- The system does not delete any of the SQL script files that you have previously generated for a screen.
        
         
        back to top
        
         
         
        SQL Formatter
        You can use this utility to have a SQL statement you enter properly formatted. For long queries, the utility will put new lines between the segments of the query.

        SQL Processor
        You can use this utility to launch the SQL Processor mini-application. The SQL Processor is used 
 to store SQL statements, run them, and save the results.
         
        General Actions
        
            To create a 
 statement to be saved, select "--NEW--" from the Name 
 drop down box.  Fill 
 in the name, active flag, and SQL in the boxes.  Then 
 select the Add button. 
            To update a 
 statement, select the statement to be modified from the Name drop 
 down box.  The 
 SQL and active flag can be modified.  When 
 you are done with the modifications, select the Update button. 
            To delete a 
 statement, select the statement from the Name drop down box.  Select 
 the Delete Button. 
            To run a statement, 
 select the statement from the Name drop down box.  A 
 statement can also be typed into the SQL box without creating a statement. 
  Select 
 the Run button to execute the statement. 
            To save the 
 results of an executed statement, go to 'File->Save Results'. 
  A window 
 will open to let you choose the file path and name. 
            To save a group 
 of SQL statements to be loaded or run at a later date, select 'File->Save 
 SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name. 
            To load a set 
 of SQL statements, select 'File->Load SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name.
        
        When running this application from the command line there are three 
 command options:
        
            /ini <filename>This option will open the application with the specified filename as 
 the .ini file.  If 
 this option is not used, the default of SQLProcessor.ini will be used. 
            /sql <filename>This will open the application will the SQL statements in the specified 
 file preloaded.  If 
 no .sql file is specified, the application will be run with no preloaded 
 statements. 
            /nThis will run the application in non-interactive mode.  When 
 in non-interactive mode, the application will run the loaded SQL statements. 
  The results 
 will be save according to the configurations set in the .ini file that 
 was specified.  If 
 there is no .sql file specified, no commands will be run.  The 
 results will be saved with the name of the command, the date, and the 
 time concatenated.  If 
 there is an error running the SQL statement, the error will be reported 
 in the file.  If 
 there was an error saving the file, it will be reported in "Error.txt" 
 in the same folder as the application. An example of invoking this is the following:  ilstoolbox 
 "SQL Processor" /sql  <filename> 
 /n NOTE: If you would like to store your SQL files in a location other 
 than where the ILSToolbox.exe is located you will need to indicate the 
 file path along with the file name when running the utility via the command 
 line.
        
        Steps to Schedule queries on SQL processor
        
            Create the SQL file through SQL processor which has to be scheduled.

Select New from the Name drop down and write the SQL query to be run in the text box. Give a name for the query in the text box under the ‘Name’ text box and Click Add.If you have multiple queries, keep adding by clicking New and following the similar steps.
Once all the queries are added, click File | Save SQL and save the file.
For example, if there were 2 queries, the contents of the SQL file would look like this:
USERPROFILE SELECT * FROM USER_PROFILE (NOLOCK) Y ¬
WAREHOUSE SELECT * FROM WAREHOUSE (NOLLOCK) Y ¬
            Settings on SQL processor. Click the Settings tab, the SQL Processor Config UI comes up; Check the output type as CSV and click Save and Exit.Copy the SQLProcessor.Default.ini file to folder where the SQL file was saved earlier. 
(Note that the default ini location is in isolated storage, where the path is like: C:\Documents and Settings\<username>\Local Settings\Application Data\IsolatedStorage\<gibberish>\<more gibberish>\StrongName.<yet even more gibberish>\AssemFiles\SQLProcessorFile.Default.ini. Or it could be found in user’s Document’s folder)

 
The Contents of the ini file would look like – 
 CSV,  which means the output file will be saved in csv format.
            Create a batch file to run the SQL query using SQL processor. In the command, put the location of the ToolBox, then the location of the sql file which was created in Step 1. Specify the location of the ini file. The SQL processor will creates the output according to the ini file settings.The command would be like this:

"C:\Program Files\Manhattan Associates\WarehouseMgt\wmtoolbox" "SQL Processor" 
/sql "C:\Manhattan\queries\Scheduled SQL Processor\ScheduleQuery.sql" /ini "C:\Manhattan\queries\Scheduled SQL Processor\SQLProcessor.ini" /n
            Create a scheduled task to run the batch file. Go to Control Panel->Scheduled Tasks-> Add new Scheduled Task.
The Scheduled Task Wizard comes up
.Click Next. On the next window Click Browse and select the batch file you have created, Select the frequency at which this job has to be done and Click Next.
 In the Next screen give the date and time at which it is required to run and Click Next.
 
On the next screen give the user name/ password information for which the task has to be run.
 
Click the Finish button in the next screen. 

The queries will be run at the scheduled time and resulting CSV files will be saved in the same folder where the batch file is present with timestamp.

        You can use this utility to generate a script for the system configuration 
 database tables.

Using Toolbox Utilities

        
The following is a comprehensive list of all the "Toolbox Utilities" 
 that are shipped with the application. In general, the purpose of these 
 utilities is to quickly perform a function in SCALE or a third-party application. 
 These are especially helpful if for some reason you need to add/manipulate 
 data outside of the application. You can access the Toolbox on the application server: Start 
 | All Programs | Manhattan Associates | ILS | Tools. You can also 
 access the toolbox by navigating to the following path on your application 
 server:          \\AppServer\ILS\, and 
 opening the file "ILSToolbox.exe"

        
 

        
**IMPORTANT** - Please run the SCALE Toolbox as an Administrative user.

        
 

        
WARNING! Do not use these utilities 
 unless you are a Manhattan representative, OR you are absolutely sure 
 of the consequences of executing a certain utility. Key application data 
 could be lost by the misuse of toolbox utilities.

        
 

        
 

        
Utility Descriptions...

        
 

        
Data Loading Utilities
            

                
 

                
NOTE: These "data loading" utilities are to be used for generating test data quickly. They are not meant to be used in a production environment for any purpose (with the exception of the Generic Config and Security utilities).

 Data Loading Utilities...

        
Containers

        
 

        
You can use this utility to create shipping containers based 
 on the allocation requests that are already in the database. This can be helpful to create containers when a wave fails prior to work creation.

        
 

        
This Utility...

        

            
Creates a single container with multiple details, if the details have the same packing class. 





            
Creates separate containers, if the details have different packing classes.





            
Puts the created container in an In Packing status.





            
The wave number you enter must 
 be a valid wave in the system. So, if you want to test only a few 
 allocation requests and put them on a test wave, be sure to create a new 
wave (with no shipments assigned) in the Wave Insight screen.

        

        
Procedures

        

            
Enter an existing wave number into the field.





            
Press the Create Containers Button. The utility will create containers in the SCALE database based on the allocation requests that already exist for the associated wave.

        

        
back to top
        

        
 

        
 

        
Customers

        
You can use this utility to create a range of customers and/or 
 ship to's. Note that one record each for customer/company combination

        

            
Enter a range of customer numbers.





            
Enter a range of ship to numbers.





            
Select the company(s) that you want to associate with these new customers/ship to's.





            
Select the country:



- If you choose United States as a country, the appropriate postal codes will be derived from the state(s) you choose.



- If you choose a country that is not United States, you will need to enter in a postal code range.





            
Press the Create Button. The system will create the appropriate customer/ship to value(s) in the CUSTOMER database table.



Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.

        

        
Address Value Notes

City is populated by the text "City".

 window.

        

            
Enter a Record Type and Description.

Press the Clear SQL Button to delete any SQL code in the toolbox window.



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.

In the Quantity Adjustment fields, enter the quantity range and unit of measure that you want to adjust.





            
In the Item/Company fields, select the item(s) that you want to adjust.





            
Press the Adjust Inventory Button to adjust the inventory quantity into the location(s). The data is placed into the LOCATION_INVENTORY database table.



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.



Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

Items

        
You can use this utility to create a new item record, and assign permanent locations and units of measure to this item. Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE Item, Item Unit of Measure, and Item Location Assignment configurations.

        

            
Enter the item or range of items that you want to create.





            
Use the tab fields to indicate the details of the item you are going to create. 



- Note that on the Values tab, when you enter minimum/maximum values for cost/price fields, the system will as a result assign a random price value (chosen as a number between these two values) for these fields on the new Item record.





            
Enter values into the Item Location Assignment tab if you want to assign a permanent location to this item.





            
Enter values into the Item Unit of Measure tab if you want to create quantity unit of measures for this item.





            
Use the Quantity of Each Permutation to be Grouped Together Field to indicate that you want the system to create a number of different permutations of the same item (i.e. company, allocation rule, NMFC). Therefore, if there is a value in this field, the system will loop through that many times, and try to create that number of different permutations (with different company based on the company values that are selected in that check list box). Once the system reaches the number of permutations indicated, it will move onto the next item and repeat this process.





            
Press the Create Button to create the item records. The data will be placed into the ITEM, ITEM_LOCATION_ASSIGNMENT, and ITEM_UNIT_OF_MEASURE database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple item records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen. 



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.



Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

        

        
back to top
        

        
 

        
 

        
Receipts

        
You can use this utility to create receipts and/or receipt lines.  Note that this utility will allow you to create receipt lines that do not match the receipt's company designation. This can cause problems when processing receipts created with this utility.

        

            
Use the General Setup fields to enter the receipt information.



- The Receipt Prefix ID Field indicates the alphanumeric string you want to appear at the beginning of your receipt IDs.





            
Use the Receipts/Details fields to enter in how many receipts you want to create, and how many lines you want on each of these receipts. 



- The Receipt ID Start Index Field indicates the number that will be added to the end of the IDs of your receipt(s). For example, if your receipt prefix ID was "TEST", and your start index was "2", if you created three receipts, they would be named "TEST-2", "TEST-3", and "TEST-4."



- Note that the system will randomly choose a number of lines that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.





            
Assign vendor/ship from/company value(s) for the receipt(s). 





            
Select the item(s) you want to include on your receipt(s). 



- Press the Non Item Master Item Button to add item(s) that are not defined in SCALE to your receipt(s). You will be able to enter the item ID, description, cost, list price, and net price for these items. After you provide this data, the non item master item will be displayed in the item list and available for selection.



- Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity value that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.





            
Press the Create Receipts Button to create the receipt(s). The data will be placed into the RECEIPT_HEADER and RECEIPT_DETAIL database tables. Note that when the tool creates multiple receipt records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.



Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

Security

        
You can use this utility to perform actions on security permissions records.  Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE Security configuration. The data this utility affects is from the SECURITY database table.

        

            
Use the Copy Security function to copy the existing security permissions of one user to another existing user. The system will copy the permissions from the user selected in the drop-down field to the user(s) who are selected in the checkbox list.
