Shipments

        
You can use this utility to create shipments and/or lines.  Essentially, this utility performs the same functions as the SCALE Shipment and Shipment Line Screens. Note that this utility will allow you to create shipment lines that do not match the shipment's company designation. This can cause problems when processing shipments created with this utility.

        

            
Use the General Setup fields to enter the shipment information.



- The Shipment Prefix ID Field indicates the alphanumeric string you want to appear at the beginning of your shipment IDs.





            
Use the Shipments/Details fields to enter in how many shipments you want to create, and how many details you want on each of these shipments. Note that the system will randomly choose a number of details that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.



- The Shipment ID Start Index Field indicates the number that will be added to the end of the IDs of your shipment(s). For example, if your shipment prefix ID was "TEST", and your start index was "2", if you created three shipments, they would be named "TEST-2", "TEST-3", and "TEST-4."





            
Assign a customer/ship to/company value(s) for the shipment(s). 





            
Select the carrier /carrier service you want associated with the shipment(s).





            
Select the item(s) you want to include on your shipment(s). 



- Press the Non Item Master Item Button to add item(s) that are not defined in SCALE to your shipment(s). You will be able to enter the item ID, description, cost, list price, and net price for these items. After you provide this data, the non item master item will be displayed in the item list and available for selection.



- Note that the system will randomly choose a quantity value that falls between the minimum/maximum you provide.





            
Choose if you want to create shipments, orders, or both. 





            
Press the Create Shipments Button to create the shipment(s). The data will be placed into the SHIPMENT_HEADER/SHIPMENT_DETAIL and/or the ORDER_HEADER/ORDER_DETAIL database tables (depending on what you selected in step 6). Note that when the tool creates multiple shipment records, the system cycles through the value criteria in the order that they were chosen.



Press the Reset Button to clear all the values selected in the data fields.



Press the View Errors Button to display any error messages that the system generated.

        

        
back to top
        

        
 

        
 

        
Work

        
You can use this utility to create work based on an existing 
 wave. Note that the system will automatically detect what type of work it should be generating. This is based on the wave flow associated with the "launch number" (wave number) which you key-in to generate the work. This utility is helpful if you need to create work for a wave that has failed prior to the work creation wave step.

        
 

        
back to top
        

        
 

        
 

        
 

        
Database Upgrade

        
You can use this utility to upgrade both the SCALE application 
 and system databases. The 
 upgrade can be from a base release to service pack, a service pack to 
 a base release, and a base release to the next base release. You can compare the environments in the list to the version listed in the header portion of the window to see if the environment(s) needs updating.

        
 

        
Application Section

        

            
Version: This field Indicates the release version of SCALE.





            
Service Pack: This field is not currently supported.

Metadata Screen Utility

        
You can use this utility to generate SQL script files in order create custom metadata screens, and activate/deactivate/delete these screens. This is helpful, if, for example, you want to create a specialized version of an Insight screen. 

        
 

        
Customizing a Base Metadata Screen

        
This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a base (shipped) metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to create a specialized version of a base metadata screen. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).

        

            
Select the Base button (note that you cannot export custom screens).





            
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.





            
Select the Metadata Screen you want to customize.





            
Press the Customize button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>.



Notes:

- As part of the Customize action, the system also will execute the SQL script that was generated. This will create all the records in the appropriate metadata configuration tables in the database.

        

        
Exporting a Custom Metadata Screen

        
This action allows you to have the system generate a SQL script file for a customized metadata screen. This is helpful if you want to save a backup of a custom screen’s current state. This script file contains SQL for the metadata screen (from the MAIN_UI_SCREEN database table all the way down the configuration tree to the other related configuration tables).

        

            
Select the Custom button (note that you cannot export base screens).





            
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.





            
Select the Metadata Screen you want to export. 





            
Press the Export button. The system will generate the SQL Script file, and display a success message. The system will place this file in the following directory: \\<AppServer>\ILS\_Custom\Export\<EnvironmentName>. 



Notes:

- This directory is created upon the first export action, not by the application installer. 



- The system will append a suffix of “V1” to the file name, which indicates this is the first version of the script file for this metadata screen. When you perform an Export action again for this screen, the system will create another “version” of the SQL script file (V2, for example). 



- The file name starts with the Form ID of the metadata screen that you exported. 



- The system will always create a new version of a file when exporting, whether or not there have been changes made to the configurations since the last export of this screen.

        

        
Activating a Customized Metadata Screen

        
This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen available for use on your production environment.

        

            
 Select the Custom button (you cannot activate base screens).





            
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.





            
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to activate.





            
Press the Activate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "Yes", and display a success message.



Notes:

- Keep in mind that when you activate a custom screen, then the system will also deactivate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you activate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will deactivate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.

        

        
Deactivating a Customized Metadata Screen

        
This action allows you to make a newly-customized metadata screen not available for use on your production environment.

        

            
 Select the Custom button (you cannot deactivate base screens).





            
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.





            
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to deactivate.





            
Press the Deactivate button.  The system will change the Active Field on all related metadata configuration records for this screen to "No", and display a success message.



Notes:

- Keep in mind that when you deactivate a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you deactivate a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.

        

        
Deleting a Customized Metadata Screen

        
This action allows you to remove a customized metadata screen’s configuration records from the database.

        

            
Select the Custom button (you cannot delete base screens).





            
Select an Environment. The system will load all of the existing custom screens into the Metadata screen field.





            
Select the Metadata Screen that you want to delete.





            
Press the Delete button.  The system will display a confirmation message, asking if you are sure you want to delete the screen. Once you confirm, the system will remove this screen’s configuration records from all of the appropriate database tables, and display a success message.



Notes:

- Keep in mind that when you delete a custom screen, then the system will also activate the related base metadata screen. For example, if you delete a custom Shipment Insight screen, then the system will activate the shipped version of the Shipment Insight screen.



- Also as part of this action, the system will generate a SQL Script file representing the deleted screen, so that you have a backup in case you want to restore it at a later time.



- The system does not delete any of the SQL script files that you have previously generated for a screen.

SQL Processor

        
You can use this utility to launch the SQL Processor mini-application. The SQL Processor is used 
 to store SQL statements, run them, and save the results.

        
 

        
General Actions

        

            
To create a 
 statement to be saved, select "--NEW--" from the Name 
 drop down box.  Fill 
 in the name, active flag, and SQL in the boxes.  Then 
 select the Add button.

 

            
To update a 
 statement, select the statement to be modified from the Name drop 
 down box.  The 
 SQL and active flag can be modified.  When 
 you are done with the modifications, select the Update button.

 

            
To delete a 
 statement, select the statement from the Name drop down box.  Select 
 the Delete Button.

 

            
To run a statement, 
 select the statement from the Name drop down box.  A 
 statement can also be typed into the SQL box without creating a statement. 
  Select 
 the Run button to execute the statement.

 

            
To save the 
 results of an executed statement, go to 'File->Save Results'. 
  A window 
 will open to let you choose the file path and name.

 

            
To save a group 
 of SQL statements to be loaded or run at a later date, select 'File->Save 
 SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name.

 

            
To load a set 
 of SQL statements, select 'File->Load SQL'.  A 
 window will open to let you choose the file path and name.

        

        
When running this application from the command line there are three 
 command options:

        

            
/ini <filename>

This option will open the application with the specified filename as 
 the .ini file.  If 
 this option is not used, the default of SQLProcessor.ini will be used.

 

            
/sql <filename>

This will open the application will the SQL statements in the specified 
 file preloaded.  If 
 no .sql file is specified, the application will be run with no preloaded 
 statements.

 

            
/n

This will run the application in non-interactive mode.  When 
 in non-interactive mode, the application will run the loaded SQL statements. 
  The results 
 will be save according to the configurations set in the .ini file that 
 was specified.  If 
 there is no .sql file specified, no commands will be run.  The 
 results will be saved with the name of the command, the date, and the 
 time concatenated.  If 
 there is an error running the SQL statement, the error will be reported 
 in the file.  If 
 there was an error saving the file, it will be reported in "Error.txt" 
 in the same folder as the application. An example of invoking this is the following:  ilstoolbox 
 "SQL Processor" /sql  <filename> 
 /n NOTE: If you would like to store your SQL files in a location other 
 than where the ILSToolbox.exe is located you will need to indicate the 
 file path along with the file name when running the utility via the command 
 line.

        

        
Steps to Schedule queries on SQL processor

        

            
Create the SQL file through SQL processor which has to be scheduled.

Select New from the Name drop down and write the SQL query to be run in the text box. Give a name for the query in the text box under the ‘Name’ text box and Click Add.



If you have multiple queries, keep adding by clicking New and following the similar steps.
Once all the queries are added, click File | Save SQL and save the file.




For example, if there were 2 queries, the contents of the SQL file would look like this:
USERPROFILE SELECT * FROM USER_PROFILE (NOLOCK) Y ¬


WAREHOUSE SELECT * FROM WAREHOUSE (NOLLOCK) Y ¬





            
Settings on SQL processor. Click the Settings tab, the SQL Processor Config UI comes up; Check the output type as CSV and click Save and Exit.



Copy the SQLProcessor.Default.ini file to folder where the SQL file was saved earlier. 
(Note that the default ini location is in isolated storage, where the path is like: C:\Documents and Settings\<username>\Local Settings\Application Data\IsolatedStorage\<gibberish>\<more gibberish>\StrongName.<yet even more gibberish>\AssemFiles\SQLProcessorFile.Default.ini. Or it could be found in user’s Document’s folder)

 




The Contents of the ini file would look like – 
 CSV,  which means the output file will be saved in csv format.





            
Create a batch file to run the SQL query using SQL processor. In the command, put the location of the ToolBox, then the location of the sql file which was created in Step 1. Specify the location of the ini file. The SQL processor will creates the output according to the ini file settings.



The command would be like this:

"C:\Program Files\Manhattan Associates\WarehouseMgt\wmtoolbox" "SQL Processor" 




/sql "C:\Manhattan\queries\Scheduled SQL Processor\ScheduleQuery.sql" 



/ini "C:\Manhattan\queries\Scheduled SQL Processor\SQLProcessor.ini" /n





            
Create a scheduled task to run the batch file. Go to Control Panel->Scheduled Tasks-> Add new Scheduled Task.
The Scheduled Task Wizard comes up
.



Click Next. On the next window Click Browse and select the batch file you have created, Select the frequency at which this job has to be done and Click Next.
 



In the Next screen give the date and time at which it is required to run and Click Next.
 




On the next screen give the user name/ password information for which the task has to be run.
 




Click the Finish button in the next screen. 





The queries will be run at the scheduled time and resulting CSV files will be saved in the same folder where the batch file is present with timestamp.
